summary_text:
On September 4, 2023, the patient was involved in a two-vehicle, heavy side-impact motor vehicle collision. EMS (Paramedic James Vance, NREMT-P) arrived to find the patient requiring mechanical extrication with jaws-of-life, with GCS 14 and mild altered mental status. Field assessment noted an odor of alcohol and a reported history of alcohol consumption prior to driving; the patient later stated she had consumed two beers at lunch. EMS applied a cervical collar with spine boarding, splinted and dressed the left arm, and noted a compound (open) fracture of the left humerus with active bleeding, a left wrist/forearm spiral deformity with severe swelling, and left-sided pain. She was transported Code 3 to Littel Inc Emergency Hospital.

On ED arrival, serum ethanol was elevated at 110 mg/dL. Exam by Dr. Elizabeth Foster documented a 2cm superficial left scalp laceration, severe cervical tenderness and muscle spasm at C4-C7, an open mid-shaft humerus fracture, a weak radial pulse with delayed capillary refill and decreased distal sensation in the left forearm/wrist, a left knee contusion, and mild lumbar paraspinal tenderness. Labs showed leukocytosis (WBC 14.2) and mildly low hemoglobin (12.8). Imaging revealed a displaced compound mid-shaft left humerus fracture with 2.2cm overriding, a displaced spiral distal radius fracture with intra-articular extension, and cervical spine findings at C5-C6 (6mm disc bulge, disc narrowing, mild retrolisthesis, onset inconclusive per radiology) with C4-C6 prevertebral soft tissue swelling consistent with acute trauma. Tdap was given, IV Ancef and pain management were initiated, and a nerve block was performed; a CT head without contrast (9/5) was negative for acute findings requiring intervention beyond monitoring.

Notably, prior records show a September 2022 cervical strain from heavy squat lifting, with imaging then showing a 4mm C5-C6 disc bulge without fracture or stenosis, treated conservatively with PT and NSAIDs.

On September 7, 2023, Dr. Myrtle Turner performed left upper extremity reconstruction: dynamic plate fixation (ORIF) of the left humerus and volar plate fixation of the left distal radius, with repair of the extensor tendon sheath (4-0 Vicryl) under fluoroscopic guidance, assisted by Dr. Charles Vance. Hospital course included IV Ancef, Ibuprofen, Dilaudid and oxycodone for pain, and PT-assisted ambulation. She was discharged September 8, 2023, on oxycodone-acetaminophen and a 6-month, 3x/week PT plan for the shoulder, arm, wrist, and cervical spine.

Outpatient follow-up through March 2024 documented persistent radial nerve sensory deficit, wrist extension weakness, progression of the C5-C6 disc bulge to 6mm with foraminal stenosis (December 2023), and eventual near-complete bony fusion by February 2024. PT at Lang-Weimann (30 sessions) was interrupted by three no-show appointments in November 2023 before resuming. Subsequent PT continued at Emory Sports through March 2024. MMI was declared March 14, 2024, with permanent 15-degree elbow and 20-degree wrist deficits, permanently blunted radial sensation, a 20-lb lifting restriction, and chronic neck pain, with cervical decompression or pain management recommended April 2, 2024.
